1.w: My son, if you have been surety for your neighbor, [or] have struck your hand for the stranger,

2.w: [or] have been lured by the words of your mouth, captured by the words of your mouth,

3.w: then you must do this my son, and deliver yourself, for you have come into the palm of your neighbor: Go humble yourself, and press your neighbor.

4.w: You should not give sleep to your eyes or slumber to your eyelids—

5.w: snatch yourself like a gazelle from the hand, and like a bird from the hand of the fowler.

6.w: Go to the ant, O sluggish one; see her ways and become wise:

7.w: Which there is not unto her a chief, an official, or ruler,

8.w: she prepares her bread in summer, she has gathered her food in the harvest.

9.w: Until when, O sluggish one, will you slumber? When will you rise from your sleep?

10.w: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to lie down,

11.w: and your poverty comes like one walking, and your need like a man of shield.

12.w: A man of worthlessness, a man of iniquity, is walking [with] crookedness of mouth,

13.w: winking with his eyes, speaking with his foot, pointing with his fingers,

14.w: [with] perversity in his heart, plotting evil; at every time he sends forth strife.

15.w: Upon thus his calamity shall come suddenly; in an instant he will be shattered, and without healing.

16.w: These six [things] YHWH hates, and seven [are] an abomination to His soul:

17.w: Eyes raised high, a tongue of falsehood, and hands pouring out innocent blood,

18.w: a heart devising plans of iniquity, feet hurrying to run toward evil,

19.w: one breathing out lies, a witness of falsehood, and one sending forth contentions between brothers.

20.w: Keep, my son, the command of your father, and do not forsake the instruction of your mother.

21.w: Bind them upon your heart continually; tie them around your neck.

22.w: In your going about, it will lead you; in your lying down, it will guard you; when you awake, it will speak with you.

23.w: For the command [is] a lamp, and the instruction a light, and the reproofs of discipline are the way to life,

24.w: to guard you from the woman of evil, from the smoothness of the tongue of a strange woman.

25.w: Do not desire her beauty in your heart, and do not let her take hold of you with her eyelids.

26.w: For the price of a woman prostitute is as a crust of bread, and the woman of a man hunts a precious soul.

27.w: Can a man seize fire in his bosom, and his garments not be burned?

28.w: Or [can] a man walk upon the hot coals, and his feet not be scorched?

29.w: So [is] the one coming in to the wife of his neighbor; anyone who touches her shall not be innocent.

30.w: They do not despise the thief if he steals to fill his soul when he is hungry,

31.w: and having been found, he must repay sevenfold; all the wealth of his house he must give.

32.w: The one committing adultery with a woman is lacking of heart; he does it, destroying his own soul.

33.w: He finds [only a stroke and shame, and his reproach is not wiped away.

34.w: For jealousy is the heat of a man, and he will not spare on the day of vengeance.

35.w: He will not lift the face of any ransom, and he will not consent, though you may multiply the bribe.
